shloka_text: तच्छ्रुत्वा भाषितं तस्य शत्रुघ्नस्य महात्मनः । क्रोधामाहारयत्तीव्रं तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति चाब्रवीत् ।। 7.69.1 ।।
transliteration: tacchrutvā bhāṣitaṃ tasya śatrughnasya mahātmanaḥ | krodhāmāhārayattīvraṃ tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti cābravīt || 7.69.1 ||
translation: तत् that, श्रुत्वा having heard, भाषितं speech, तस्य his, शत्रुघ्नस्य of Shatrughna, महात्मनः the great-souled, क्रोधं anger, आहारयत् he felt, तीव्रं intense, तिष्ठ stop, तिष्ठ stop, इति thus, च and, अब्रवीत् he said
explanation: Having heard that speech of the great-souled Shatrughna, he felt intense anger and exclaimed, "Stop! Stop!"
comments: The battle resumes -- Lavana hurls trees and fells Shatrughna senseless, but, thinking him dead, fails to fetch his trident -- recovering, Shatrughna takes up the divine arrow, whose blazing splendour terrifies all beings until Brahma reveals it to be Vishnu's own form -- Shatrughna looses it into Lavana's chest and slays him, the trident returns to Rudra, and the gods rejoice at the death of the world's terror.

shloka_text: पाणौ पाणिं विनिष्पिष्य दन्तान्कटकटाय्य च । लवणो रघुशार्दूलमाह्वयामास चासकृत् ।। 7.69.2 ।।
transliteration: pāṇau pāṇiṃ viniṣpiṣya dantānkaṭakaṭāyya ca | lavaṇo raghuśārdūlamāhvayāmāsa cāsakṛt || 7.69.2 ||
translation: पाणौ in hand, पाणिं hand, विनिष्पिष्य having pressed, दन्तान् teeth, कटकटाय्य having gnashed, च and, लवणो Lavaṇa, रघुशार्दूलम् the tiger among Raghus (Shatrughna), आह्वयामास challenged, च and, असकृत् repeatedly.
explanation: Lavaṇa, pressing his hands together and gnashing his teeth, repeatedly challenged Shatrughna, the foremost of the Raghu dynasty.

shloka_text: तं ब्रुवाणं तथा वाक्यं लवणं घोरदर्शनम् । शत्रुघ्नो देवशत्रुघ्न इदं वचनमब्रवीत् ।। 7.69.3 ।।
transliteration: taṃ bruvāṇaṃ tathā vākyaṃ lavaṇaṃ ghoradarśanam | śatrughno devaśatrughna idaṃ vacanamabravīt || 7.69.3 ||
translation: तं him, ब्रुवाणं speaking, तथा such, वाक्यं words, लवणं Lavaṇa, घोरदर्शनम् of terrible appearance, शत्रुघ्नो Shatrughna, देवशत्रुघ्न the destroyer of the gods' enemy, इदं this, वचनम् word, अब्रवीत् spoke.
explanation: To Lavaṇa, who was speaking such words and had a terrible appearance, Shatrughna, the destroyer of the gods' enemy, spoke these words.

shloka_text: न शत्रुघ्नस्तथा जातो यथा ऽन्ये निर्जितास्त्वया । तदद्य बाणाभिहतो व्रज त्वं यमसादनम् ।। 7.69.4 ।।
transliteration: na śatrughnastathā jāto yathā 'nye nirjitāstvayā | tadadya bāṇābhihato vraja tvaṃ yamasādanam || 7.69.4 ||
translation: न not, शत्रुघ्नस्तथा Shatrughna is such, जातो born, यथा as, अन्ये others, निर्जितास्त्वया conquered by you, तदद्य therefore today, बाणाभिहतो struck by arrows, व्रज go, त्वं you, यमसादनम् to the abode of Yama.
explanation: Shatrughna declared that he was not like the others Lavaṇa had conquered, and therefore, Lavaṇa would today be struck by his arrows and go to the abode of Yama.

shloka_text: ऋषयो ऽप्यद्य पापात्मन्मया त्वां निहतं रणे । पश्यन्तु विप्रा विद्वांसस्त्रिदशा इव रावणम् ।। 7.69.5 ।।
transliteration: ṛṣayo 'pyadya pāpātmanmayā tvāṃ nihataṃ raṇe | paśyantu viprā vidvāṃsastridaśā iva rāvaṇam || 7.69.5 ||
translation: ऋषयो sages, अप्यद्य also today, पापात्मन् O evil-souled one, मया by me, त्वां you, निहतं slain, रणे in battle, पश्यन्तु let them see, विप्रा Brahmins, विद्वांसः learned ones, त्रिदशाः gods, इव like, रावणम् Ravana.
explanation: Shatrughna wished that the sages, Brahmins, and learned ones, like the gods witnessing Ravana's fall, would today see him slay the evil-souled Lavaṇa in battle.

shloka_text: त्वयि मद्बाणनिर्दग्धे पतिते ऽद्य निशाचर । पुरे जनपदे चापि क्षेममेव भविष्यति ।। 7.69.6 ।।
transliteration: tvayi madbāṇanirdagdhe patite 'dya niśācara | pure janapade cāpi kṣemameva bhaviṣyati || 7.69.6 ||
translation: त्वयि you, मद्बाणनिर्दग्धे burnt by my arrows, पतिते fallen, अद्य today, निशाचर O night-wanderer, पुरे in the city, जनपदे in the country, च and, अपि also, क्षेममेव welfare indeed, भविष्यति will be.
explanation: Shatrughna declared that with Lavaṇa, the night-wanderer, burnt by his arrows and fallen today, there would indeed be welfare in both the city and the country.

shloka_text: अद्य मद्बाहुनिष्क्रान्तः शरो वज्रनिभाननः । प्रवेक्ष्यते ते हृदयं पद्ममंशुरिवार्कजः ।। 7.69.7 ।।
transliteration: adya madbāhuniṣkrāntaḥ śaro vajranibhānanaḥ | pravekṣyate te hṛdayaṃ padmamaṃśurivārkajaḥ || 7.69.7 ||
translation: अद्य today, मद्बाहुनिष्क्रान्तः issued from my arm, शरः arrow, वज्रनिभाननः having a thunderbolt-like tip, प्रवेक्ष्यते will enter, ते your, हृदयम् heart, पद्मम् a lotus, अंशुः a ray, इव like, अर्कजः of the sun,
explanation: Today, the arrow released from my arm, with its thunderbolt-like tip, will pierce your heart just as a sunbeam penetrates a lotus.

shloka_text: एवमुक्तो महावृक्षं लवणः क्रोधमूर्च्छितः । शत्रुघ्नोरसि चिक्षेप स च तं शतधाच्छिनत् ।। 7.69.8 ।।
transliteration: evamukto mahāvṛkṣaṃ lavaṇaḥ krodhamūrcchitaḥ | śatrughnorasi cikṣepa sa ca taṃ śatadhācchinat || 7.69.8 ||
translation: एवम् thus, उक्तः addressed, महावृक्षम् a great tree, लवणः Lavana, क्रोधमूर्च्छितः overcome with anger, शत्रुघ्नोरसि on Shatrughna's chest, चिक्षेप threw, सः he, च and, तम् that, शतधा into a hundred pieces, अच्छिनत् cut,
explanation: Thus addressed, Lavana, overcome with rage, hurled a massive tree at Shatrughna's chest, but Shatrughna instantly shattered it into a hundred pieces.

shloka_text: तद्दृष्ट्वा विफलं कर्म राक्षसः पुनरेव तु । पादपान्सुबहून्गृह्य शत्रुघ्नायासृजद्बली ।। 7.69.9 ।।
transliteration: taddṛṣṭvā viphalaṃ karma rākṣasaḥ punareva tu | pādapānsubahūngṛhya śatrughnāyāsṛjadbalī || 7.69.9 ||
translation: तत् that, दृष्ट्वा having seen, विफलम् fruitless, कर्म action, राक्षसः the demon, पुनरेव again indeed, तु and, पादपान् trees, सुबहून् very many, गृह्य seizing, शत्रुघ्नाय at Shatrughna, असृजत् hurled, बली the powerful one,
explanation: Seeing that action prove fruitless, the powerful demon Lavana again seized very many trees and hurled them at Shatrughna.

shloka_text: शत्रुघ्नश्चापि तेजस्वी वृक्षानापततो बहून् । त्रिभिश्चतुर्भिरेकैकं चिच्छेद नतपर्वभिः ।। 7.69.10 ।।
transliteration: śatrughnaścāpi tejasvī vṛkṣānāpatato bahūn | tribhiścaturbhirekaikaṃ ciccheda nataparvabhiḥ || 7.69.10 ||
translation: शत्रुघ्नः Shatrughna, च and, अपि also, तेजस्वी powerful, वृक्षान् trees, आपततः falling, बहून् many, त्रिभिः with three, चतुर्भिः with four, एकैकम् each one, चिच्छेद cut, नतपर्वभिः with bent-jointed arrows,
explanation: And the powerful Shatrughna, with his bent-shafted arrows, cut down each of the many approaching trees with three or four arrows.

shloka_text: ततो बाणमयं वर्षं व्यसृजद्राक्षसोरसि । शत्रुघ्नो वीर्यसम्पन्नो विव्यथे न स राक्षसः ।। 7.69.11 ।।
transliteration: tato bāṇamayaṃ varṣaṃ vyasṛjadrākṣasorasi | śatrughno vīryasampanno vivyathe na sa rākṣasaḥ || 7.69.11 ||
translation: ततः then, बाणमयम् a shower of arrows, वर्षम् rain, व्यसृजत् discharged, राक्षसोरसि on the demon's chest, शत्रुघ्नः Shatrughna, वीर्यसम्पन्नः endowed with valor, विव्यथे was pained, न not, सः that, राक्षसः demon,
explanation: Then, the valorous Shatrughna unleashed a shower of arrows upon the demon's chest, but that demon was not pained by them.

shloka_text: ततः प्रहस्य लवणो वृक्षमुद्यम्य वीर्यवान् । शिरस्यभ्यहनच्छूरं स्रस्ताङ्गः स मुमोह वै ।। 7.69.12 ।।
transliteration: tataḥ prahasya lavaṇo vṛkṣamudyamya vīryavān | śirasyabhyahanacchūraṃ srastāṅgaḥ sa mumoha vai || 7.69.12 ||
translation: ततः then, प्रहस्य having laughed, लवणो Lavana, वृक्षम् a tree, उद्यम्य having lifted, वीर्यवान् the mighty one, शिरसि on the head, अभ्यहनत् struck, शूरम् the brave one, स्रस्ताङ्गः with limbs loosened, सः he, मुमोह fainted, वै indeed.
explanation: Then, the mighty Lavana laughed, lifted a tree, and struck the brave Shatrughna on the head, causing him to faint with his limbs loosened.

shloka_text: तस्मिन्निपतिते वीरे हाहाकारो महानभूत् । ऋषीणां देवसङ्घानां गन्धर्वाप्सरसां तथा ।। 7.69.13 ।।
transliteration: tasminnipatite vīre hāhākāro mahānabhūt | ṛṣīṇāṃ devasaṅghānāṃ gandharvāpsarasāṃ tathā || 7.69.13 ||
translation: तस्मिन् when that, निपतिते fell down, वीरे brave one, हाहाकारो a cry of distress, महान् great, अभूत् arose, ऋषीणाम् of the sages, देवसङ्घानाम् of the hosts of gods, गन्धर्वाप्सरसां of Gandharvas and Apsaras, तथा and also.
explanation: When that brave warrior fell, a great cry of distress arose from the sages, hosts of gods, Gandharvas, and Apsaras.

shloka_text: तमवज्ञाय तु हतं शत्रुघ्नं भुवि पातितम् । रक्षो लब्धान्तरमपि न विवेश स्वमालयम् ।। 7.69.14 ।।
transliteration: tamavajñāya tu hataṃ śatrughnaṃ bhuvi pātitam | rakṣo labdhāntaramapi na viveśa svamālayam || 7.69.14 ||
translation: तम् him, अवज्ञाय disregarding, तु but, हतम् killed, शत्रुघ्नम् Shatrughna, भुवि on the ground, पातितम् fallen, रक्षो the demon, लब्धान्तरमपि even though having found an opportunity, न not, विवेश entered, स्वमालयम् his own abode.
explanation: Disregarding Shatrughna, who had fallen to the ground as if killed, the demon, even though he had found an opportunity, did not enter his own abode.

shloka_text: नापि शूलं प्रजग्राह तं दृष्ट्वा भुवि पातितम् । ततो हत इति ज्ञात्वा तान्भक्षान्समुदावहत् ।। 7.69.15 ।।
transliteration: nāpi śūlaṃ prajagrāha taṃ dṛṣṭvā bhuvi pātitam | tato hata iti jñātvā tānbhakṣānsamudāvahat || 7.69.15 ||
translation: न not, अपि even, शूलम् the trident, प्रजग्राह took up, तम् him, दृष्ट्वा having seen, भुवि on the ground, पातितम् fallen, ततः then, हतः killed, इति thus, ज्ञात्वा having known, तान् those, भक्षान् food items, समुदावहत् carried away.
explanation: Even after seeing Shatrughna fallen on the ground, Lavana did not pick up his trident; instead, thinking him dead, he carried away his prey.

shloka_text: मुहूर्ताल्लब्धसञ्ज्ञस्तु पुनस्तस्थौ धृतायुधः । शत्रुघ्नो वै पुरद्वारि ऋषिभिः सम्प्रपूजितः ।। 7.69.16 ।।
transliteration: muhūrtāllabdhasañjñastu punastasthau dhṛtāyudhaḥ | śatrughno vai puradvāri ṛṣibhiḥ samprapūjitaḥ || 7.69.16 ||
translation: मुहूर्तात् in a moment, लब्धसञ्ज्ञस्तु having regained consciousness, पुनः again, तस्थौ stood, धृतायुधः holding his weapon, शत्रुघ्नः Shatrughna, वै indeed, पुरद्वारि at the city gate, ऋषिभिः by the sages, सम्प्रपूजितः well-worshipped.
explanation: In a moment, Shatrughna regained consciousness, and, holding his weapon, he stood again at the city gate, honored by the sages.

shloka_text: ततो दिव्यममोघं तं जग्राह शरमुत्तमम् । ज्वलन्तं तेजसा घोरं पूरयन्तं दिशो दश ।। 7.69.17 ।।
transliteration: tato divyamamoghaṃ taṃ jagrāha śaramuttamam | jvalantaṃ tejasā ghoraṃ pūrayantaṃ diśo daśa || 7.69.17 ||
translation: ततः then, दिव्यम् divine, अमोघम् unfailing, तम् that, जग्राह he took, शरम् arrow, उत्तमम् excellent, ज्वलन्तम् blazing, तेजसा with splendor, घोरम् dreadful, पूरयन्तम् filling, दिशः directions, दश ten.
explanation: Then he took that excellent, divine, and unfailing arrow, which was blazing with dreadful splendor and filling all ten directions.

shloka_text: वज्राननं वज्रवेगं मेरुमन्दरसन्निभम् । नतं पर्वसु सर्वेषु संयुगेष्वपराजितम् ।। 7.69.18 ।।
transliteration: vajrānanaṃ vajravegaṃ merumandarasannibham | nataṃ parvasu sarveṣu saṃyugeṣvaparājitam || 7.69.18 ||
translation: वज्राननम् having a tip like a thunderbolt, वज्रवेगम् having the speed of a thunderbolt, मेरुमन्दरसन्निभम् resembling Mount Meru and Mandara, नतम् bent, पर्वसु at the joints, सर्वेषु all, संयुगेषु in battles, अपराजितम् unconquered.
explanation: The arrow had a thunderbolt-like tip and speed, resembled Mount Meru and Mandara, was perfectly bent at all its joints, and remained unconquered in all battles.

shloka_text: असृक्चन्दनदिग्धाङ्गं चारुपत्रं पतत्रिणम् । दानवेन्द्राचलेन्द्राणामसुराणां च दारणम् ।। 7.69.19 ।।
transliteration: asṛkcandanadigdhāṅgaṃ cārupatraṃ patatriṇam | dānavendrācalendrāṇāmasurāṇāṃ ca dāraṇam || 7.69.19 ||
translation: असृक् blood, चन्दन sandalwood, दिग्धाङ्गम् smeared on its body, चारुपत्रम् having beautiful feathers, पतत्रिणम् winged, दानवेन्द्र of the lords of Danavas, अचलेन्द्राणाम् of the lords of mountains, असुराणाम् of Asuras, च and, दारणम् a splitter.
explanation: Its body was smeared with blood and sandalwood, it had beautiful feathers, and it was capable of splitting the lords of Danavas, the lords of mountains, and the Asuras.

shloka_text: तं दीप्तमिव कालाग्निं युगान्ते समुपस्थिते । दृष्ट्वा सर्वाणि भूतानि परित्रासमुपागमन् ।। 7.69.20 ।।
transliteration: taṃ dīptamiva kālāgniṃ yugānte samupasthite | dṛṣṭvā sarvāṇi bhūtāni paritrāsamupāgaman || 7.69.20 ||
translation: तम् that, दीप्तम् blazing, इव like, कालाग्निम् the fire of destruction, युगान्ते at the end of an age, समुपस्थिते having arrived, दृष्ट्वा having seen, सर्वाणि all, भूतानि beings, परित्रासम् great fear, उपागमन् they experienced.
explanation: Seeing that arrow blazing like the fire of destruction at the end of a cosmic age, all beings were struck with great terror.

shloka_text: सदेवासुरगन्धर्वं मुनिभिः साप्सरोगणम् । जगद्धि सर्वमस्वस्थं पितामहमुपस्थितम् ।। 7.69.21 ।।
transliteration: sadevāsuragandharvaṃ munibhiḥ sāpsarogaṇam | jagaddhi sarvamasvasthaṃ pitāmahamupasthitam || 7.69.21 ||
translation: सदेवासुरगन्धर्वम् with gods, asuras, and gandharvas, मुनिभिः with sages, साप्सरोगणम् with groups of Apsaras, जगत् the world, हि indeed, सर्वम् all, अस्वस्थम् uneasy, पितामहम् to Brahma, उपस्थितम् approached.
explanation: Indeed, the entire world, including gods, asuras, gandharvas, sages, and groups of Apsaras, became uneasy and approached Brahma.

shloka_text: उवाच देवदेवेशं वरदं प्रपितामहम् । देवानां भयसंमोहो लोकानां सङ्क्षयं प्रति ।। 7.69.22 ।।
transliteration: uvāca devadeveśaṃ varadaṃ prapitāmaham | devānāṃ bhayasaṃmoho lokānāṃ saṅkṣayaṃ prati || 7.69.22 ||
translation: उवाच said, देवदेवेशं to the lord of gods, वरदं the bestower of boons, प्रपितामहम् to the great-grandfather, देवानां of the gods, भयसंमोहो fear and bewilderment, लोकानां of the worlds, सङ्क्षयं destruction, प्रति regarding.
explanation: The gods addressed Brahma, the great-grandfather and bestower of boons, regarding the fear and bewilderment among the gods and the impending destruction of the worlds.

shloka_text: नेदृशं दृष्टपूर्वं च न श्रुतं प्रपितामह । देवानां भयसम्मोहो लोकानां सङ्क्षयं प्रति ।। 7.69.23 ।।
transliteration: nedṛśaṃ dṛṣṭapūrvaṃ ca na śrutaṃ prapitāmaha | devānāṃ bhayasammoho lokānāṃ saṅkṣayaṃ prati || 7.69.23 ||
translation: न not, ईदृशं such, दृष्टपूर्वं seen before, च and, न not, श्रुतं heard, प्रपितामह O great-grandfather, देवानां of the gods, भयसम्मोहो fear and bewilderment, लोकानां of the worlds, सङ्क्षयं destruction, प्रति regarding.
explanation: They declared to Brahma that such fear and bewilderment among the gods, concerning the destruction of the worlds, had never been seen or heard of before.

shloka_text: तेषां तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा ब्रह्मा लोकपितामहः । भयकारणमाचष्ट लोकानामभयङ्करः । उवाच मधुरां वाणीं शृणुध्वं सर्वदेवताः ।। 7.69.24 ।।
transliteration: teṣāṃ tadvacanaṃ śrutvā brahmā lokapitāmahaḥ | bhayakāraṇamācaṣṭa lokānāmabhayaṅkaraḥ | uvāca madhurāṃ vāṇīṃ śṛṇudhvaṃ sarvadevatāḥ || 7.69.24 ||
translation: तेषां their, तत् that, वचनं speech, श्रुत्वा having heard, ब्रह्मा Brahma, लोकपितामहः the great-grandfather of the worlds, भयकारणम् the cause of fear, आचष्ट explained, लोकानाम् of the worlds, अभयङ्करः the dispeller of fear, उवाच said, मधुरां sweet, वाणीं words, शृणुध्वं listen, सर्वदेवताः O all gods.
explanation: Having heard their words, Brahma, the great-grandfather and dispeller of fear for the worlds, explained the cause of their fear and spoke sweet words, asking all the gods to listen.

shloka_text: वधाय लवणस्याजौ शरः शत्रुघ्नधारितः । तेजसा तस्य सम्मूढाः सर्वे स्मः सुरसत्तमाः ।। 7.69.25 ।।
transliteration: vadhāya lavaṇasyājau śaraḥ śatrughnadhāritaḥ | tejasā tasya sammūḍhāḥ sarve smaḥ surasattamāḥ || 7.69.25 ||
translation: वधाय for the killing, लवणस्य of Lavana, आजौ in battle, शरः the arrow, शत्रुघ्नधारितः held by Shatrughna, तेजसा by the radiance, तस्य of that, सम्मूढाः bewildered, सर्वे all, स्मः we are, सुरसत्तमाः O best of gods.
explanation: Brahma revealed that the gods' bewilderment was caused by the immense radiance of the arrow held by Shatrughna, intended for the killing of Lavana in battle.

shloka_text: एष पूर्वस्य देवस्य लोककर्तुः सनातनः । शरस्तेजोमयो वत्सा येन वै भयमागतम् ।। 7.69.26 ।।
transliteration: eṣa pūrvasya devasya lokakartuḥ sanātanaḥ | śarastejomayo vatsā yena vai bhayamāgatam || 7.69.26 ||
translation: एष this, पूर्वस्य of the ancient, देवस्य god, लोककर्तुः the creator of the worlds, सनातनः eternal, शरः arrow, तेजोमयः full of light, वत्सा O dear ones, येन by which, वै indeed, भयम् fear, आगतम् has come.
explanation: Brahma further explained that this radiant arrow, which caused their fear, is the eternal weapon of the ancient god, the creator of the worlds.

shloka_text: एष वै कैटभस्यार्थे मधुनश्च महाशरः । सृष्टो महात्मना तेन वधार्थे दैत्ययोस्तयोः ।। 7.69.27 ।।
transliteration: eṣa vai kaiṭabhasyārthe madhunaśca mahāśaraḥ | sṛṣṭo mahātmanā tena vadhārthe daityayostayoḥ || 7.69.27 ||
translation: एषः this, वै indeed, कैटभस्य of Kaitabha, अर्थे for the sake of, मधुनः of Madhu, च and, महाशरः great arrow, सृष्टः created, महात्मना by the great-souled one, तेन by him, वधार्थे for the purpose of killing, दैत्ययोः of the two demons, तयोः those two,
explanation: This great arrow was indeed created by that great-souled one for the purpose of killing those two demons, Kaitabha and Madhu.

shloka_text: एक एव प्रजानाति विष्णुस्तेजोमयं शरम् । एषा एव तनुः पूर्वा विष्णोस्तस्य महात्मनः ।। 7.69.28 ।।
transliteration: eka eva prajānāti viṣṇustejomayaṃ śaram | eṣā eva tanuḥ pūrvā viṣṇostasya mahātmanaḥ || 7.69.28 ||
translation: एकः only one, एव indeed, प्रजानाति knows, विष्णुः Vishnu, तेजोमयम् full of splendor, शरम् arrow, एषा this, एव indeed, तनुः body, पूर्वा ancient, विष्णोः of Vishnu, तस्य of that, महात्मनः great-souled one,
explanation: Only Vishnu truly knows this arrow, which is full of splendor, for this is indeed the ancient form of that great-souled Vishnu himself.

shloka_text: इतो गच्छत पश्यध्वं वध्यमानं महात्मना । रामानुजेन वीरेण लवणं राक्षसोत्तमम् ।। 7.69.29 ।।
transliteration: ito gacchata paśyadhvaṃ vadhyamānaṃ mahātmanā | rāmānujena vīreṇa lavaṇaṃ rākṣasottamam || 7.69.29 ||
translation: इतः from here, गच्छत go, पश्यध्वम् see, वध्यमानम् being killed, महात्मना by the great-souled one, रामानुजेन by Rama's younger brother, वीरेण by the hero, लवणम् Lavana, राक्षसोत्तमम् the chief of Rakshasas,
explanation: Go from here and witness Lavana, the chief of Rakshasas, being killed by the great-souled hero, Rama's younger brother.

shloka_text: तस्य ते देवदेवस्य निशम्य वचनं सुराः । आजग्मुर्यत्र युध्येते शत्रुघ्नलवणावुभौ ।। 7.69.30 ।।
transliteration: tasya te devadevasya niśamya vacanaṃ surāḥ | ājagmuryatra yudhyete śatrughnalavaṇāvubhau || 7.69.30 ||
translation: तस्य his, ते that, देवदेवस्य of the God of gods, निशम्य having heard, वचनम् words, सुराः the gods, आजग्मुः came, यत्र where, युध्येते were fighting, शत्रुघ्नलवणौ Shatrughna and Lavana, उभौ both,
explanation: Having heard the words of that God of gods, the deities arrived at the place where both Shatrughna and Lavana were engaged in battle.

shloka_text: तं शरं दिव्यसङ्काशं शत्रुघ्नकरधारितम् । ददृशुः सर्वभूतानि युगान्ताग्निमिवोत्थितम् ।। 7.69.31 ।।
transliteration: taṃ śaraṃ divyasaṅkāśaṃ śatrughnakaradhāritam | dadṛśuḥ sarvabhūtāni yugāntāgnimivotthitam || 7.69.31 ||
translation: तम् that, शरम् arrow, दिव्यसङ्काशम् divine-looking, शत्रुघ्नकरधारितम् held in Shatrughna's hand, ददृशुः saw, सर्वभूतानि all beings, युगान्ताग्निम् the fire of the end of an age, इव like, उत्थितम् risen,
explanation: All beings saw that divine-looking arrow, held in Shatrughna's hand, shining like the risen fire of the cosmic dissolution.

shloka_text: अकाशमावृतं दृष्ट्वा देवैर्हि रघुनन्दनः । सिंहनादं भृशं कृत्वा ददर्श लक्षणं पुनः ।। 7.69.32 ।।
transliteration: akāśamāvṛtaṃ dṛṣṭvā devairhi raghunandanaḥ | siṃhanādaṃ bhṛśaṃ kṛtvā dadarśa lakṣaṇaṃ punaḥ || 7.69.32 ||
translation: अकाशम् the sky, आवृतम् covered, दृष्ट्वा having seen, देवैः by gods, हि indeed, रघुनन्दनः Shatrughna, सिंहनादम् a lion's roar, भृशम् loudly, कृत्वा having made, ददर्श he saw, लक्षणम् Lakshmana, पुनः again.
explanation: Indeed, having seen the sky covered by gods, Shatrughna, after letting out a loud lion's roar, saw Lakshmana again.

shloka_text: आहूतश्च पुनस्तेन शत्रुघ्नेन महात्मना । लवणः क्रोधसंयुक्तो युद्धाय समुपस्थितः ।। 7.69.33 ।।
transliteration: āhūtaśca punastena śatrughnena mahātmanā | lavaṇaḥ krodhasaṃyukto yuddhāya samupasthitaḥ || 7.69.33 ||
translation: आहूतः called, च and, पुनः again, तेन by him, शत्रुघ्नेन by Shatrughna, महात्मना the great-souled, लवणः Lavana, क्रोधसंयुक्तः filled with anger, युद्धाय for battle, समुपस्थितः stood ready.
explanation: And again, challenged by the great-souled Shatrughna, Lavana, filled with anger, appeared ready for battle.

shloka_text: आकर्णात्स विकृष्याथ तद्धनुर्धन्विनां वरः । तं मुमोच महाबाणं लवणस्य महोरसि ।। 7.69.34 ।।
transliteration: ākarṇātsa vikṛṣyātha taddhanurdhanvināṃ varaḥ | taṃ mumoca mahābāṇaṃ lavaṇasya mahorasi || 7.69.34 ||
translation: आकर्णात् up to the ear, सः he, विकृष्य having drawn, अथ then, तत् that, धनुः bow, धन्विनाम् among archers, वरः the best, तम् that, मुमोच he released, महाबाणम् great arrow, लवणस्य of Lavana, महोरसि on the great chest.
explanation: Then, the best among archers, Shatrughna, having drawn that bow up to his ear, released that great arrow onto Lavana's broad chest.

shloka_text: उरस्तस्य विदार्याशु प्रविवेश रसातलम् ।। 7.69.35 ।।
transliteration: urastasya vidāryāśu praviveśa rasātalam || 7.69.35 ||
translation: उरः the chest, तस्य his, विदार्य having pierced, आशु quickly, प्रविवेश it entered, रसातलम् the netherworld.
explanation: Quickly piercing his chest, the arrow entered the netherworld.

shloka_text: गत्वा रसातलं दिव्यः शरो विबुधपूजितः । पुनरेवागमत्तूर्णमिक्ष्वाकुकुलनन्दनम् ।। 7.69.36 ।।
transliteration: gatvā rasātalaṃ divyaḥ śaro vibudhapūjitaḥ | punarevāgamattūrṇamikṣvākukulanandanam || 7.69.36 ||
translation: गत्वा having gone, रसातलम् to the netherworld, दिव्यः divine, शरः arrow, विबुधपूजितः worshipped by gods, पुनरेव again indeed, आगमत् it came, तूर्णम् quickly, इक्ष्वाकुकुलनन्दनम् to the delight of the Ikshvaku family.
explanation: Having gone to the netherworld, the divine arrow, worshipped by gods, quickly returned to Shatrughna, the delight of the Ikshvaku family.

shloka_text: शत्रुघ्नशरनिर्भिन्नो लवणः स निशाचरः । पपात सहसा भूमौ वज्राहत इवाचलः ।। 7.69.37 ।।
transliteration: śatrughnaśaranirbhinno lavaṇaḥ sa niśācaraḥ | papāta sahasā bhūmau vajrāhata ivācalaḥ || 7.69.37 ||
translation: शत्रुघ्नशरनिर्भिन्नो pierced by Shatrughna's arrow, लवणः Lavana, सः that, निशाचरः demon, पपात fell, सहसा suddenly, भूमौ on the ground, वज्राहतः struck by a thunderbolt, इव like, अचलः a mountain.
explanation: That demon Lavana, pierced by Shatrughna's arrow, suddenly fell to the ground like a mountain struck by a thunderbolt.

shloka_text: तच्च शूलं महत्तेन हते लवणराक्षसे । पश्यतां सर्वदेवानां रुद्रस्य वशमन्वगात् ।। 7.69.38 ।।
transliteration: tacca śūlaṃ mahattena hate lavaṇarākṣase | paśyatāṃ sarvadevānāṃ rudrasya vaśamanvagāt || 7.69.38 ||
translation: तत् that, च and, शूलम् trident, महत् great, तेन by him, हते having been killed, लवणराक्षसे Lavana the demon, पश्यताम् while watching, सर्वदेवानाम् of all the gods, रुद्रस्य of Rudra, वशम् to the control, अन्वगात् returned.
explanation: And that great trident, after the demon Lavana was killed by Shatrughna, returned to the control of Rudra while all the gods watched.

shloka_text: एकेषुपातेन भृशं निपात्य लोकत्रयस्यापि रघुप्रवीरः । विनिर्बभावुत्तमचापबाणस्तमः प्रणुद्येव सहस्ररश्मिः ।। 7.69.39 ।।
transliteration: ekeṣupātena bhṛśaṃ nipātya lokatrayasyāpi raghupravīraḥ | vinirbabhāvuttamacāpabāṇastamaḥ praṇudyeva sahasraraśmiḥ || 7.69.39 ||
translation: एकेषुपातेन by the shot of a single arrow, भृशम् completely, निपात्य having struck down, लोकत्रयस्य of the three worlds, अपि even, रघुप्रवीरः the great hero of the Raghu dynasty, विनिर्बभौ shone forth, उत्तमचापबाणः with an excellent bow and arrow, तमः darkness, प्रणुद्य having dispelled, इव like, सहस्ररश्मिः the sun.
explanation: Having completely struck down the terror of the three worlds with a single arrow, the great hero of the Raghu dynasty, Shatrughna, shone forth with his excellent bow and arrow, just like the sun dispelling darkness.

shloka_text: ततो हि देवा ऋषिपन्नगाश्च प्रपूजिरे ह्यप्सरसश्च सर्वाः । दिष्ट्या जयो दाशरथेरवाप्तस्त्यक्त्वा भयं सर्प इव प्रशान्तः ।। 7.69.40 ।।
transliteration: tato hi devā ṛṣipannagāśca prapūjire hyapsarasaśca sarvāḥ | diṣṭyā jayo dāśaratheravāptastyaktvā bhayaṃ sarpa iva praśāntaḥ || 7.69.40 ||
translation: ततः then, हि indeed, देवाः gods, ऋषि sages, पन्नगाः serpents, च and, प्रपूजिरे worshipped, हि indeed, अप्सरसः Apsaras, च and, सर्वाः all, दिष्ट्या fortunately, जयः victory, दाशरथेः of Dasharatha's son, अवाप्तः obtained, त्यक्त्वा having abandoned, भयम् fear, सर्पः a serpent, इव like, प्रशान्तः calmed.
explanation: Then indeed, all the gods, sages, serpents, and Apsaras worshipped him, exclaiming that fortunately, victory had been obtained by Dasharatha's son, and they were now calm, having abandoned fear, like a pacified serpent. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे एकोनसप्ततितमः सर्गः ।। 69 ।। Thus ends the sixty-ninth sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
